items.title: Is the moral panic over Grand Theft Auto valid?
paras: Every time a controversial video game hits the market, the moral panic returns.
It was no different when, on International Men’s Day, Grand Theft Auto VI dropped after more than a decade of development. The game made $4 billion in 24 hours. What cost-of-living crisis, eh?

Thanks to time zone magic, New Zealand was the first nation to unlock the game, resulting in players employing the ‘New Zealand Trick’ to switch their location while the most devoted fans flew to Mordor to play it live.

Millions of men around the world were struck down with ‘GTA Flu’. The mystery ‘pandemic’ was most pronounced amongst men in their 20s, although the World Health Organisation is yet to make an official comment.

Grand Theft Auto has been controversial since its first iteration in 1997 (MS-DOS, Windows) and 1999 (PlayStation, Game Boy). However, it was Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas (2004) that attracted serious controversy. It contained significant escalations in criminality and sexual content involving what was, at the time, hyper-realistic graphics.

This is where the conversation switched from ‘game play’ to ‘role play’. We are still having this discussion as technology creates ever-more convincing simulations of reality, especially in terms of AI generating footage of real people.

Generally speaking, Grand Theft Auto requires players to engage in mandatory activities centring on criminality: vigilante missions, pimping out women, burglary, and (obviously) grand theft auto. It also includes strip clubs and hookers. San Andreas was never accused of being ‘Woke’. Immediately upon release, it became a target for social justice activists who seemed more concerned about its portrayal of racial stereotypes than its glorification of ‘thug life’.
Most young men today grew up with Grand Theft Auto V , released in 2013, which was reviewed as ‘one of the best video games ever made’ and ‘generation-defining’.
As the most ‘morally lenient’ entry in the franchise, the game was so controversial that two major department stores in Australia pulled it from their shelves.

That sort of boycotting does not work today, where games are downloaded directly from the console. This is a shame for game stores. PlayStation announced all of its new releases will be essentially download-only. The rest of the industry is set to follow. Gone are the days where you can hold a physical copy of your games. Younger generations before digital formats. I hate them. It makes it too easy for distributers and governments to erase your purchases, introduce additional fees, or edit the content post-sale.

And who knows, how long before our eSafety Commissioner, and others like her, start monitoring in-game activity for problematic behaviour? We never thought they would do it to our social media use, and yet people are getting knocks on the door for tweets.

The prevalence of social media has meant higher visibility for the content of Grand Theft Auto VI . Clips are doing the rounds showing men walking up to women only to beat them to death, shoot them in the head, and rob them. With uncanny valley realism, video game violence makes for uncomfortable viewing.
It was easier to write-off gaming violence as harmless fantasy when it wasn’t so realistic. Does realism make these games more harmful? Maybe.

I say this as a gaming girl who grew up playing Doom II when I was seven years old and Tomb Raider not long after that. There was a moral panic surrounding those games too, but if I am being completely honest, these older video games were a very different species.

Far from ‘damaging attention spans’, early video game players often found themselves trapped in puzzle rooms for days or having to memorise hours of gameplay to escape levels with no save points. Children of my generation reported exceptional hand-eye coordination as a direct result and longer attention spans. Doom II was so convoluted that the game was not fully completed, by anyone, until Zero-Master in 2018. (I can still regurgitate these cheat codes with greater accuracy than my maths formulas.)

These games, thanks to a combination of story, graphics, and game-style, did not interfere with people’s experience of reality. The line between the game and the real world was not easily blurred for the ordinary user. In this case, I argued firmly that the moral panic over the video game era was total nonsense, just like the moral panic over Harry Potter.

These new games are not the same. They monetise and encourage short-attention spans, instant gratification, and escalations in realistic violence and criminal behaviour to generate a ‘thrill’. True problem solving is limited.

Worse, we already live in a world with a youth crime problem, largely thanks to the impact of rap culture. The concern is that games glorifying crime could make the situation worse for parents. Keep in mind, governments across the West have banned children from social media (allegedly to keep them safe from harmful content) and yet we know young boys are playing these adult-rated games.

I am a social media enthusiast and old gamer, yet I would not play Grand Theft Auto . The experience is similar to being a movie fan who does not enjoy excessive realistic gore in horror. Not all films are the same and not all games are the same.

This is not a call to ban anything, more of a conversation starter about what direction our society is heading in when it comes to its dominant form of entertainment. Why do men seek these games out. What are they getting from them as adults? Why is this game the best seller?

Gaming used to be a relatively niche group, and most gamers spent the majority of their time in the real world. The structure of society in the 80s and 90s forced young people to balance their lives between gaming, education requirements, and the responsibility of young adulthood.

I remain disturbed by scenes of young adults throwing violent tantrums when parents try to remove them from gaming. Or of adults ignoring their responsibility as parents to stream on Twitch for hours every day.

That sort of behaviour represents a deeper level of emotional dependency and immaturity rarely seen in classic gaming. Something has obviously changed, although I suspect soft parenting has a lot to do with the problem.

Children are biologically wired into addiction-forming habits. It is a side-effect of our species’ advanced learning ability. Extreme focus on a particular task is how humans mastered skills like hunting (before being eaten). In a modern setting, this can translate into addictive gaming and obsessive relationships when not properly moderated by parents.
Political decisions have complicated the problem for parents and children.

For kids these days, the outside world is often as dangerous as Grand Theft Auto VI . If you live in Melbourne, there’s a good chance you’ll face a machete-wielding gang of teenagers at the local shopping centre, or be woken up by child home invaders stealing keys for a bit of real grand theft auto of the family car. That is not the world I experienced as a child after a few hours playing Doom II .
What are the (mostly male) gamers learning and what sort of adults will the become?

I remember the issue being discussed when Call of Duty , and all of its sequels, came out. At least Call of Duty taught players a significant amount of political and war history. They learned the fine details of weapons and essential military information. If playing online, they organised teams in combat situations where the delegated tasks and acted as a cohesive unit. I was astonished watching a young relative of mine play this game in which he took command of an international group, running missions with extraordinary organisational skills across multiple time zones.

Those kids could tell you more about warfare than most professors (and they sure as heck did not learn it from school). War is also a likely problem many men will face, and so there is a solid argument that these games are just as beneficial as military training. Certainly, it readies them emotionally for critical thinking in tactical situations.

Heck, perhaps Elon Musk should finance the Call of Duty team to make a war game set in Mao’s revolution or life under Stalin. Set a level in the farmlands where people were buried alive or eating their own children. Host another level on Cannibal Island. It could challenge players to survive socialism, dodge the regime’s secret police, and overthrow history’s tyrannical dictators. They could call it Orwell . I guarantee it would be the fastest way to inoculate Western youth against the disease of collectivism. A viral anti-socialist game would be the end of left-wing politics.

With Grand Theft Auto, people are asking, where is the benefit of a criminal fantasy world? Escapism, perhaps. Do I think there should be guardrails? Yes. Most people do. Where is your line of decency? Beating and killing random women on the street; shooting up gay bars (as some complained they could not do); anything involving children … most people who say they do not believe in ‘lines in the sand’ actually do have them.

Despite all this, the actual response from people who are playing the game does not quite fit the stereotype. If we ignore the AI-generated rage-bait posts and feminists who oppose the content on principle, there appears to be a few observations worth making.

Many have criticised the game for being Woke. By that they mean too much of the gameplay revolves around domestic tasks while the criminality of previous games has been restrained. There are viral clips showing the main character fixing a sink or grocery shopping. One reviewer wrote:

‘I was surprised that, with about 10-plus hours of play, most of my time has been spent performing mundane tasks like home repair, grocery shopping, personal grooming, and trying to open a bank account. The realism is incredible, but perhaps too real.’

They appeared to be happy with this immersion in a fabricated world, (then again, the reviewer listed his age as 59), but other younger players were furious. It is clear that the game has embedded subliminal messaging for young men in regards to building a healthy relationship with their partner, while increasing punishments for violent criminal behaviour that dominated previous games.

With the quality of graphics and extended open maps, the experience reported by men playing together in groups is that of an alternate reality, like The Sims . (Some of you might remember when that took over people’s lives, especially young girls.)

It made me wonder how many men, starved of their masculinity in this post-feminist world, throw money at games like Grand Theft Auto VI because it is one of the last male-coded activities available to them away from the prying, judgemental eyes of the state. You cannot be judged for your behaviour while playing the game, (at least, not yet!).

I’ve read many men say how sad it is to watch adults take time off work to sit in a dark room, ignore their partners and children, all so they can role-play criminals in a game. There is some merit to that view, but it is linked to the way men feel about their jobs and future in the first place. Most Western men, particularly in countries like Australia, will never fight, never break the law, and they will probably never hold a gun. Having been exposed to superhero narratives and action movies through their childhood, their real lives can seem docile in comparison.
Alexandra Marshall is an independent writer. If you would like to support her work, shout her a coffee over at donor-box .

items.title: Eyre Peninsula residents worried about further blackouts
paras: Transmission tower and powerlines down at Wharminda. ( Supplied: Chris Prime )
Eyre Peninsula residents say they are counting on temporary fixes to the power grid to carry them through the next few weeks.
About 24,000 properties were without power on Thursday during a mass blackout.
The region is now temporarily being serviced by the mothballed Port Lincoln power station and reconfigured power lines.
An intense storm damaged three transmission towers, which operator ElectraNet said crippled the "radial line" powering much of the peninsula, including Port Lincoln.
Storm clouds above grain fields on the Eyre Peninsula where wild weather lashed the region on Thursday afternoon ( Supplied: Benjamin Wandel )
The company is investigating whether any structural defects were to blame but said that it is unlikely.
Port Lincoln mayor Diana Mislov acknowledged the severe weather was "an unexpected event" but wanted assurances that the construction requirements were met.
"I think the whole line needs to be looked at and more work undertaken to ensure that this doesn't happen again," Ms Mislov said.
Port Lincoln's Mayor Diana Mislov said she was putting her faith in the people operating the regional city's mothballed power station. ( Robert Lang )
"I understand the cost-benefit analysis that needs to happen with some of this decision-making, but we can't afford to allow our communities to be without power."
The nearby power plant, which is privately owned and will shut down permanently in 2028, will be used for several days, according to ElectraNet.
Ms Mislov wanted to see the plant maintained long-term as a back-up option.
"The fact we were able to fire up the power station … and get it back into action for our communities is incredibly important," she said.
She also urged people who had lost power to switch off their solar panels, in line with SA Police's instructions, to avoid overloading the grid.
On Friday, Premier Peter Malinauskas also warned that predicted storm events and hot weather on Sunday could further strain the grid.
The Bureau of Meteorology is predicting early thunderstorms and temperatures to reach around 30 on the Lower Eyre Peninsula.
Restaurant owner Craig McCathie, of the Fresh Fish Place, said he was concerned about more blackouts over the next few weeks while repairs are underway.
The venue's back-up generator kicked in, but Mr McCathie said a blackout running into several days – such as in 2016 – "wouldn't be a good scenario" if the town's reserves run out.
"It does cause a bit of a stress because of what's happened in the past," he said.
Fresh Fish Place owner Craig McCathie said businesses and industry in the region are dependent on reliable power. ( ABC News: Duncan Bailey )
"We keep enough [fuel] for about 20 hours, but when the town is down, the diesel pumps are down too, so we haven't got a back-up plan for when we run out of our storage."
There is still no timeline for when the damaged towers will be permanently replaced, but temporary structures are expected to go up within days, which will bolster energy reliability.
Speaking to 891 Adelaide, ElectraNet's Alex Trento said the company was confident its designs were structurally sound.
"Depending on the investigation, that'll determine whether we go down the path of looking at a different design," Mr Trento said.

"But at this point in time we're of the strong view that the design is adequate, tested to the requirements of the Australian standards ... and constructed by very competent contractors, with ElectraNet personnel overseeing [them]".

items.title: Reserve Bank issues Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) (Second Amendment) Regulations
paras: The Foreign Exchange Management (Export of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2015 were superseded by the Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026, which were issued on January 13, 2026 , and became effective from October 01, 2026. The new regulations are principle based; intended to promote ease of doing business, especially for small exporters and importers; and empower Authorised Dealers to provide quicker and more efficient service to their customers. Based on subsequent feedback received from stakeholders, the Reserve Bank has issued Amendment Regulations to Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026 that were notified on November 02, 2026 , and came into effect, retrospectively, from October 01, 2026 . In this regard, to facilitate better understanding of the new trade regulations by the exporters/importers and other stakeholders, the Reserve Bank has placed a Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on the Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026 on its website. (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-2027/1531

items.title: RBI imposes monetary penalty on Fusion Finance Limited
paras: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has, by an order dated November 17, 2026, imposed a monetary penalty of ₹7.50 lakh (Rupees Seven Lakh Fifty Thousand only) on Fusion Finance Limited (the company) for non-compliance with certain provisions of directions issued by RBI on ‘Know Your Customer (KYC)’ and ‘Internal Ombudsman’. This penalty has been imposed in exercise of powers conferred on RBI under section 58G(1)(b) read with section 58B(5)(aa) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934. The statutory inspection of the company was conducted by RBI with reference to its financial position as on March 31, 2026. Based on the supervisory findings of non-compliance with RBI directions and related correspondence in that regard, a notice was issued to the company advising it to show cause as to why penalty should not be imposed on it for failure to comply with the RBI directions. After considering the company's reply to the notice, additional submissions made by it and oral submissions made during the personal hearing, RBI found that the following charges against the company were sustained, warranting imposition of monetary penalty: The company failed to obtain PAN or equivalent e-document thereof or Form 60 from customers, while establishing an account-based relationship with those customers; and, The company failed to escalate the partly or wholly rejected complaints to the Internal Ombudsman for a final decision within the prescribed time. This action is based on deficiencies in regulatory compliance and is not intended to pronounce upon the validity of any transaction or agreement entered into by the company with its customers. Further, imposition of this monetary penalty is without prejudice to any other action that may be initiated by RBI against the company. (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-2027/1537

items.title: Indian students in Kazan delighted as PM Modi arrives for BRICS Summit
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel Kazan [ Russia ], October 22 (ANI): Indian students in Kazan , Russia , are happy and excited about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's arrival at Hotel Korston , as he attends the 16th BRICS Summit . Notably, PM Narendra Modi on Tuesday touched down in Kazan city of Russia to participate in the 16th BRICS Summit and received a warm welcome. He is here to attend the 16th BRICS Summit , being held under the Chairmanship of Russia . To welcome PM Modi , students from India studying in Russia also sang a welcome song as they awaited PM Modi 's arrival at Hotel Korston . An Indian student from Pune, Saniya said that the students are quite excited to greet PM Modi . "Maybe we will get the opportunity (to meet PM Modi ) as many students are here (at Hotel Korston )... We are very excited. We are lucky to have this opportunity and we are happy to see him," she told ANI. An Indian student from Bihar, Shaurya Pratap said, "We are very happy to welcome PM Modi and we have prepared a song for him and we hope he likes it." Surbhi from Delhi said, "I have been here in Kazan since 2019 and today, we are going to sing a song for PM Modi and we are very excited about that." Parul, a final-year medical student, who has been in Kazan for the last five years told ANI, "We are really grateful that we got this opportunity to welcome our dear Prime Minister." Arti Pawar from Maharashtra said, "I have been living here for the past three years. I am very happy that PM Modi is coming here." Mrunmayi from Nagpur, Maharashtra said, "All the students here are quite enthusiastic as PM is going to come soon. We are too much delighted to welcome him." Meanwhile, ISKCON volunteers - from the Russia n and Indian communities were seen chanting 'Hare Krishna, Hare Ram' ahead of PM Modi 's arrival. While speaking with ANI, Sergoy, an ISKCON volunteer, said, "'Hare Krishna is a Mahamantra. This visit of PM Modi to Kazan , Russia is an important one for us. We are happy." Another ISKCON volunteer said, "We want to welcome PM Modi here in Kazan . It's a great honour for us to welcome him here We are very excited to see him." A Russia n citizen, Alexander said that the people there will welcome PM Modi by singing a song and that he is happy with PM Modi 's visit to Kazan . He said, "We have made a banner and we will also sing a song to welcome PM Modi ... I returned from India just two days back and directly came from Delhi to Kazan to see PM Modi . I am very happy that he is coming to Russia ." Notably, ahead of his departure to Russia , PM Modi shared a post on X and wrote, "Leaving for Kazan , Russia , to take part in the BRICS Summit . India attaches immense importance to BRICS, and I look forward to extensive discussions on a wide range of subjects. I also look forward to meeting various leaders there." The Prime Minister's office in a statement quoted PM Modi as saying, "I am departing today on a two-day visit to Kazan at the invitation of H.E. Mr. Vladimir Putin, President of the Russia n Federation, to attend the 16th BRICS Summit ." "India values the close cooperation within BRICS which has emerged as an important platform for dialogue and discussion on issues concerning the global developmental agenda, reformed multilateralism, climate change, economic cooperation, building resilient supply chains, promoting cultural and people to people connect, among others," PM Modi said. The statement further said that the expansion of BRICS with the addition of new members last year has added to its inclusivity and agenda for the global good. "Building upon the Annual Summit held in July 2024 in Moscow, my visit to Kazan will further reinforce the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between India and Russia . I look forward to meeting other leaders from BRICS as well," the PMO statement said. The 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan is being held under the chairmanship of Russia from October 22-24. During his visit, PM Modi is also expected to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts from BRICS member countries and invited leaders in Kazan . The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said, "The Summit, themed 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security,' will provide an important platform for leaders to discuss key global issues." It further said, "The Summit will offer a valuable opportunity to assess the progress of initiatives launched by BRICS and to identify potential areas for future collaboration." This visit marks, PM Modi 's second visit to Russia this year. He travelled to Moscow in July to attend the 22nd India- Russia Annual Summit where he held a bilateral meeting with President Putin. He was also conferred with Russia 's highest civilian award, the Order of St. Andrew the Apostle at the Kremlin in Moscow. BRIC, as a formal grouping, started after the meeting of the Leaders of Russia , India and China in St Petersburg on the margins of G8 Outreach Summit in 2006. The grouping was formalized during the first meeting of BRIC Foreign Ministers on the margins of UNGA in New York in 2006. The first BRIC Summit was held in Russia 's Yekaterinburg in 2009. It was agreed to expand BRIC into BRICS with the inclusion of South Africa at the BRIC Foreign Ministers' meeting in New York in 2010. South Africa attended the 3rd BRICS Summit in Sanya in 2011. A further expansion of BRICS took place in 2024 with five new members - Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. (ANI)

items.title: "Singapore plays key role in Act-East policy": Rajnath Singh at India-Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [ India ], October 22 (ANI): Dr. Ng Eng Hen , Singapore 's Minister of Defence , has begun his three-day visit to India . As part of his visit, Dr. Hen co-chaired the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi, with his India n counterpart Rajnath Singh . The Summit began on Tuesday morning, with India n Defence Minister Rajnath Singh welcoming the Singapore delegation warmly. He noted that the strategic partnership the two countries share is a "testimony of increasing closeness between our countries." Singh said, " The meeting is happening at a time when India marks the decade of India 's Act in Policy, in which Singapore has played a key role in promoting economic cooperation, cultural ties, and developed strategic connectivity with country institutions." Building upon Singh's remarks, Dr. Ng Eng Hen said, "You reminded us that this is the 10th year since your Act East Policy. From Singapore 's perspective, India has always been part of the East. Whether you choose to act or look, we consider you part of the area." He said that while remembering the history of Singapore , India has been an important partner. " When we started the Singapore armed forces, one of the countries that we asked early on to see whether they could help us was India ." Hen highlighted that such historical memoirs serve as important reminders and "reflects how we feel that India is very part of our area. We are delighted that our ten years of bilateral relations have been very much improved in defence and all-round strategic partnership." Hen also thanked PM Modi for visiting Singapore earlier this year and noted that the visit was an excellent meeting. A day before, the Ministry of Defence had announced the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi on October 22, 2024. The release noted that between India and Singapore , "The engagements have diversified to include wide-ranging contacts between the Services, military-to-military exchanges, high-level visits, capacity building and training programs, cooperation in UN Peacekeeping, ship visits and bilateral exercises." Inaugurated in 2016, the India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue is a key platform to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation between Singapore and India . The fifth edition of the Defence Ministers' Dialogue took place in January 2021 through virtual teleconference. During the meeting, the two parties showed confidence in the outcomes of the meeting that would result in providing impetus to the entire spectrum of the bilateral engagement as well as to the regional security architecture. (ANI)

items.title: "India matters most for future of planet" says British High Commissioner Lindy Cameron
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): In recent times when climate change has become a pressing issue with countries across the world being ravaged due to climate catastrophes, it becomes imperative to discuss and deliberate upon global actions that can help the world rise up and meet these challenges. At the NDTV World Summit's a discussion was held on the theme, "India Matters The Most For Future Of Planet". Participants in the discussion included Erik Solheim, Former Minister of Climate and the Environment of Norway; Lindy Cameron , British High Commissioner to India; Shishir Priyadarshi, President Chintan Research Foundation; Harjeet Singh, Global Engagement Director, Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative. "India is the country that matters the most for the future of the planet and climate change. India's ambition for development should not in any way be constrained by the responsibilities of the planet," Lindy Cameron , British High Commissioner to India, emphasised. She noted that the UK is committed towards the Multilateral Development Banks (MDB) reforms, technology and research support in India to aid the efforts. "Every dollar invested in resilient infrastructure pays 4 times over," said Cameron. "Lived experience of climate emergencies helps people to understand why their government needs to take policy action now," she added. Further talking about the need for urgent government action, Harjeet Singh, Global Engagement Director, Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative said, "Series of disasters affecting both developed and developing countries are serving as a wake-up call. As rich countries will get more and more affected by climate change which they did not imagine till a couple of years ago, most vulnerable countries are going to be struggling with impacts who also have very less capacity to deal with it. India is taking a leadership role in the global fight against climate change. Initiatives such as Global Biofuels Alliance, International Solar Alliance, and Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure are some efforts taken by India in recent years to manage the climate crisis. (ANI)

items.title: India is the top market for investment globally: Mark Mobius
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Mark Mobius, Founder of Mobius Capital Partners LLP , and an ace investor with expertise in emerging markets said, India's is the top stock market globally where he would like to invest. In an exclusive interview with ANI, the octagenarian said, "India would have to come first when I think about investment," Mobius stated, "Of course, India would have to be the first choice. Then, I would probably look at Taiwan. It's a Chinese society, but it's a free society and they're doing very well. Now we're beginning to see China rise again. There will be some interesting companies in China, but still, India remains our top pick." Mobius highlighted technology as his favorite sector to invest in India. "In the future, I believe there's going to be significant growth in hardware technology. As you know, India is already strong in software technology, but moving forward, hardware manufacturing will gain momentum here in India," he said. Discussing India's semiconductor infrastructure, Mobius mentioned that it is already developing. "Many of the world's large semiconductor companies already have software development operations in India, employing thousands of software engineers. The next step, of course, is hardware. Soon, we'll see large semiconductor manufacturing plants. The scale of investment we're talking about isn't in the millions, but billions of dollars, to produce the most advanced semiconductors in the world." Mobius also fondly remembered Ratan Tata, who passed away this month. "I met him many years ago and found him to be a very friendly, humble, and insightful person. I was deeply saddened to hear about his passing. I considered him one of the great Indian entrepreneurs of the century," Mobius added. Earlier on Monday, Mark Mobius, speaking at the NDTV World Summit 2024, reiterated he was bullish on India's real estate and semiconductor sectors, as he outlined the potential of these two key industries. In the semiconductor space, he said fabrication companies (fabs) will come here because India has got the population and the labour force. The octagenarian believes India will become "the leader" of the semiconductor industry. The government has so far approved five semiconductor units in India, of which construction in two sites is on, and soon the work in the other three will start. The companies have already made a cumulative investment of almost Rs 1.5 lakh crore. While talking about the parameters he looks at while investing in companies, Mobius said he looks at the growth of earnings in companies, along with the return on capital invested, and the quality of management. Asked about his investment advice to his "younger self," Mobius said, "Don't be in a rush, and study carefully". He added that one has to listen to the market. (ANI)

items.title: Mukka Proteins Limited Announces Rs 98 Crore Preferential Issue for Acquisition and Expansion
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel VMPL Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], October 22: Mukka Proteins Limited , India's largest fish meal and insect meal producer and a leader in the animal protein industry , has announced the approval of a preferential issue worth Rs 98 crore by its Board of Directors. This strategic move will help Mukka Proteins in its ongoing domestic and international acquisition and expansion efforts, reinforcing its position in the global market. A significant portion of the funding will come from the promoter and promoter group, underlining their commitment to the company's robust growth strategy. The preferential issue will comprise up to 1.96 crore equity shares at Rs50 per share, aggregating to Rs98 crore. This price includes a premium of Rs49 per share on the face value of Rs1. Mukka Proteins will use the raised capital to enhance production capabilities and meet the growing global demand for sustainable and high-quality protein solutions, particularly in the fishmeal and insect meal sectors. In a clear show of confidence, Mukka Proteins' promoters have committed to a capital infusion of INR 60 crore through a preferential allotment of equity shares. This significant financial backing will be used to strengthen the company's financial position, reduce debt, and fund key operational improvements. Mukka Proteins has consistently embraced sustainability, having commercialized insect protein as a significant innovation for the aquaculture and animal feed industry. The company's waste-to-food initiatives have contributed to environmental sustainability, particularly in collaboration with the Mangaluru municipality for waste management. These efforts not only align with global environmental best practices but also enhance circular economy processes, focusing on converting municipal waste into valuable protein and oil products. Mukka Proteins is known for its strong commitment to ecological preservation, evident through the development of sustainable products such as fishmeal, fish oil, and insect protein. As a key player in the aquaculture and nutraceutical markets, Mukka contributes 25-30% of the market share in India's fishmeal and fish oil industry. The company plans to expand its operations further, capitalizing on this capital infusion to enter new markets and enhance its global footprint.

This issuance is subject to necessary statutory and regulatory approvals, including shareholder approval at the upcoming Extra-Ordinary General Meeting (EGM) on November 16, 2024. Managing Director and CEO Harris commented, "This preferential issue is a major milestone for Mukka Proteins as we continue to strengthen our market position. Our growth plans remain firmly rooted in sustainability, and this capital will enable us to scale up production, diversify our product offerings, and reinforce our commitment to responsible and eco-friendly business practices." Mukka Proteins Limited is poised to capture new opportunities in the animal protein sector, reinforcing its legacy of innovation, sustainability, and operational excellence. Mukka Proteins Limited : Mukka Proteins Limited is a leading manufacturer and exporter of fish meal , fish oil, and other protein products. The company has built a reputation for delivering high-quality, sustainable protein products to a global customer base. With a commitment to innovation and quality, Mukka Proteins serves industries including aquaculture, pet food, and agriculture across multiple continents. Headquartered in Mangalore, India, Mukka Proteins operates state-of-the-art processing facilities that meet stringent international standards. The company is dedicated to sustainable practices and has been at the forefront of environmental stewardship within the protein processing industry. items.title: Carlos Alcaraz matches Pete Sampras’ personal record by reaching the ATP Finals semi-finals
paras: Carlos Alcaraz is already winning major titles at a rate that would see him break almost every record that came before him. After all, he recently became the youngest man in history to complete the Career Grand Slam, just a few years after he was confirmed to be the youngest-ever year-end world number one.

Year on year, this Spanish superstar seems only to be getting better and better. After 2026, it feels as though the only thing that could stop him from cementing his future status as the greatest of all time is his own body.

In the meantime, Carlos Alcaraz will continue trying to do what he does best, which is winning tennis matches and entertaining fans. He certainly has been accomplishing that so far this week, and even matched Pete Sampras ’ personal record at this particular event after beating Flavio Cobolli.

items.title: Brad Gilbert has a theory for why Carlos Alcaraz is getting injured so much, ‘not everyone can be like Federer’
paras: Carlos Alcaraz has endured an injury-riddled year, which has seen him miss more than four months of competitive action. His absence from the ATP Tour left a massive vacuum, with Alexander Zverev the generous beneficiary to his faltering fitness.

Despite the hardships endured after spending so long on the sidelines, many did predict that the Spaniard could use this rest time to return reinvigorated at the end of the season . Winning titles in Tokyo, Vienna and Paris has certainly proven that suggestion correct.

Who do you think is now taking home the ATP Finals title? That being said, it must be noted that Alcaraz has picked up a hamstring injury during his comfortable group-stage run, with Brad Gilbert looking ahead to how this might shape the tournament. Speaking on the Big T podcast , after he had previewed Carlos Alcaraz ’s upcoming semi-final vs Ben Shelton, the American pundit and coach was asked why he thinks the 23-year-old suffers so often from injury.
items.impact: Gilbert finished by reiterating that, whilst Shelton and Ferrero will want to win this match, his pre-season ahead of the Australian Open is what really matters for their new professional relationship.

items.title: Daniil Medvedev responds when asked if he doubted whether he would ever get back to where he is now
paras: Daniil Medvedev has been on a resurgence in the 2026 season, which he has continued at the ATP Finals.
Medvedev had a disappointing season by his standards last year, having dropped to as low as world number 18 and therefore failed to qualify for the ATP Finals for the first time since 2018.

There were questions over whether Medvedev, who is a former world number one, would be able to get back near to his previous best, but he has proven that he is not quite finished yet. After beating Tiafoe to secure his place in the last-four of the ATP Finals, Medvedev was asked if he ever had doubts about whether he would be able to get himself back to this point. While Medvedev suggested that there were a few doubts last year, he explained that he always knew that consistency was what he needed to do so, as he commented on Alexander Zverev’s success this year.

items.title: Flavio Cobolli claims Carlos Alcaraz is ‘by far’ the best player in the world after losing to him at the ATP Finals
paras: Flavio Cobolli was in tears earlier this week, as he lost to Frances Tiafoe at the ATP Finals. However, following his final round-robin match against Carlos Alcaraz , although the result was the same, he seemed in much better spirits.

It has been an outstanding season for the Italian, and his qualification at this prestigious end-of-year event felt wholly justified. Sadly, the jump was just too high on this occasion, though the experience should only fuel him to return reinvigorated in the future.

Who do you think is now taking home the ATP Finals title? Now, Flavio Cobolli has explained exactly how difficult it is to face the Spaniard when he’s in this kind of form. What’s particularly interesting is that, given Alcaraz recently underwent an MRI scan in relation to a hamstring injury picked up earlier this week, he’s not even at full fitness.

items.title: November 21, 1999: The day Lindsay Davenport defeated Martina Hingis to win the season-ending WTA Championships
paras: Every day, Tennis Majors looks back to the biggest moments in tennis history. On November 21, 1999, Martina Hingis’ era of dominance came to an end at the hands of Lindsay Davenport

On this day, November 21, 1999, Lindsay Davenport defeated Martina Hingis 6-4, 6-2 in the final of what was then called the WTA Chase Championships, the women’s season-ending event. This match was more evidence of Hingis’ struggles against an upcoming generation of very powerful players.

The “Swiss Miss”, aged only 19, had already won five Grand Slam titles, but she would never manage to lift another major trophy, despite three consecutive finals reached at the Australian Open (2000-2002). Lindsay Davenport was born in 1976 in the United States. The Argentine described Davenport’s game style with simple words: “She likes to hit the ball hard into the corner.

Friendships are built by repeated contact, not by being liked
items.hook: This is the single most useful fact in the whole guide.
paras: Studies of primary-school classrooms found that children seated next to each other were far more likely to become friends than children seated across the room. When teachers changed the seating, new friendships formed with the new neighbours.

So the engine is: same place, same people, same activity, over and over. The day at the yo-yo bar followed by basketball is that engine working - shared activity changed how the other boy treated him. It was not luck.
items.do: Pick one activity he already likes and commit to it weekly for a full term.

items.title: Keep the proximity - change the watching
items.hook: Your instinct is half right, and the other half matters.
paras: You are right that being around the group matters: children nominate as friends the children they see and interact with most. 'Out of sight, out of mind' is real for acquaintances.

But guidance written for schools is blunt: merely remaining beside a group is not friendship. A child who hovers is read as a bystander rather than a player, and it holds him in the one-down position. Watching has a use - but only as the first twenty seconds of joining in, never as the endpoint.
items.do: Keep telling him to stay near the group. Add: 'then take a job in the game'.

items.title: Teach 'watch, then blend'
items.hook: The best way to join a game is not to ask.
paras: Most of us were told to walk up and say 'Can I play?' But that makes everyone stop and look at him, and makes 'no' very easy.

The better sequence, used by people who study play: watch for about twenty seconds to learn the game and where the line is, then slide into the action without stopping it. Take the end of the line. Stand in the outfield. Pick up the ball and pass it back.
items.do: Rehearse it at home in five minutes. Ask him to name the 'easiest job' in each game.

items.title: Host one friend at a time - this is the biggest lever you control
items.hook: The child who invites is rarely short of friends.
paras: Pick a child he has had fun with in the last month, not someone he admires from afar. Invite one person for one to two hours. Put away anything precious, have two activities ready, start with a snack, and let the guest choose sometimes.
Keep it short and end while they are both still enjoying it. Then leave a few weeks before inviting the same child again, so the invitation can come back to him.
items.do: Text one parent this week and set a date for the school holidays.

items.title: Ask the teacher one specific question
items.hook: Teachers see the playground. Ask them to name names.
paras: Ask two things: who does he play well with, and could he be seated near them or paired with them for group work?
Seating is one of the few levers that reliably creates new friendships, and it is invisible to the children - no one has to know it was arranged.
items.do: Email the teacher this week with those two questions.

items.title: Do not push into a group that is rejecting him
items.hook: Here the advice is the opposite of persistence.
paras: Where a group is actively excluding him, the guidance is to back off - when you back off from people, they can move towards you. Put his energy into two or three other children instead of one closed circle.
Friends in more than one place - school, a club, family friends - also make him far less vulnerable when one group turns cold.
items.do: Help him list three children outside the difficult group he could get to know.

items.title: One or two good friends is the goal - not popularity
paras: Kids need one or two good friends. You do not need to worry about him being the most popular child in the class.
His warmth and kindness are already the raw material. Treat this as coaching a skill, not fixing a fault - if he feels like a project, he will resist.
items.do: Say his strengths out loud, often. Confidence is what carries a child into a group.

items.title: Playing and talking with girls is normal and good
items.hook: Children believe gender matters far more than it actually does.
paras: In one large classroom experiment, simply seating boys and girls next to each other doubled how often they became friends.
Girls' play tends to build conversation, turn-taking and inventing games together; boys' play builds bigger, faster group play. Being good at both widens his circle.
items.do: No action needed. Just do not let him think it is odd.

items.title: When to get more help
items.hook: Ordinary friendship difficulty is not a disorder.
paras: Get more support if he becomes reluctant to go to school, is persistently distressed, has changes in sleep or appetite, or says it is happening all the time and he cannot make it stop.
Start with his teacher, then the school counsellor, then your GP for a referral. Kids Helpline is free and open 24/7 on 1800 55 1800, for children and for parents.
items.do: Save Kids Helpline in your phone: 1800 55 1800.
